answer: Agents trading rarities like a plume, a cedar beam, or a marble slab must lock a refundable deposit in an on-chain escrow. Every identity needs its own deposit, so a Sybil farmer spawning thousands of fake buyers must finance thousands of bonds upfront. If a detector flags coordinated self-trading, the escrow slashes each linked deposit and burns it. Honest traders reclaim their stake plus fees; the attacker loses capital proportional to farm size, so every extra fake account raises the guaranteed loss and kills the profit.
